deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is not by Riemann. It is an editorial note in the hand of Karl Hattendorff, whose signature 'K. Hattendorff' appears on the preceding leaf. It is evidently the draft or fair copy of the editorial note printed with Riemann's paper 'Über die Fläche vom kleinsten Inhalt bei gegebener Begrenzung' in the Gesammelte mathematische Werke (1876).

Content, paraphrased:
(1) The paper on the surface of least area with given boundary is based on a Riemann manuscript. According to Riemann himself it was written in 1860 and 1861.
(2) The manuscript was extremely condensed, containing only formulas and no text.
(3) Riemann entrusted it to Hattendorff in April 1866 for elaboration.
(4) Hattendorff worked it into a paper and submitted it to the Königliche Gesellschaft der Wissenschaften zu Göttingen on 6 January 1867. It was printed in volume 13 of that society's Abhandlungen.
(5) The paper is now reprinted a second time after careful revision.
(6) When the first printing was already finished, Hattendorff received the Monatsberichte of the Berlin Academy for October and December 1866. These contain Weierstrass's paper 'Über die Flächen, deren mittlere Krümmung überall gleich Null ist'.
(7) The page breaks off at 'Wie auf dem Gebiete der Abelschen Functionen so sind also auch ...'. The next page continues: the two great mathematicians met here too, and their investigations fall at nearly the same time.

The mathematical problem in the background is the Plateau problem for minimal surfaces, i.e. surfaces of zero mean curvature. Riemann and Weierstrass both used complex-analytic or conformal representations of them; the modern name is the Enneper–Weierstrass representation. None of that is computed on this page.
errors: Historically the note is consistent with the known record. Riemann's minimal-surface paper was edited by Hattendorff and appeared in Abh. Kgl. Ges. Wiss. Göttingen 13 (1867). Weierstrass's note appeared in Monatsber. Berlin Akad. 1866. The Riemann paper was reprinted with a Hattendorff note in Riemann's Werke (1876).
The sentence 'welche im 13. Bande ... abgedruckt' lacks a finite auxiliary verb (e.g. 'ist'). This is a stylistic omission in the original, not a transcription error.
